predecessors.name: Greek Dark Ages
predecessors.text: Laconia, the Eurotas valley: Sparta's own land at the end of the Dark Age

successors.name: Achaean League
successors.text: Laconia without the coastal cities: Sparta 'forced into' the Achaean League by Philopoemen in 192 BC after Nabis was overthrown

ledger.x: -800: Sparta, a Dorian state in the Eurotas valley.
724: Messenia conquered; its people become helots.
660: the Messenians rise; the Second Messenian War.
650: the Messenian revolt crushed; Messenia remains helot land until 369.
550: Corinth joins the league ('Corinth joined c.
461: 'Megara left the League again in 461' and allied with Athens (First Peloponnesian War).
448: Megara back in the league ('It rejoined in 448'); the Thirty Years' Peace returned 'Megara... to the Peloponnesian League'.
446: Troezen 'rejoined following the Thirty Years' Peace' (winter 446–445).
421: 'Mantinea defected in 421 BCE' after the Peace of Nicias.
418: Mantineia 'rejoined after its 418 defeat' at the first battle of Mantinea.
404: the Spartan hegemony over the Aegean.
ledger.cp: Aegean cities of the former Delian League

ledger.x: 404: the occupation of Decelea ends with Athens' surrender on 25 April 404 BC.
404: Athens, defeated, is 'forced to join the League in 404'; the Thirty Tyrants, 'a reactionary regime set up by Sparta'.
395: Athens leaves the league with the Corinthian War ('Athens left in 395 BCE').
395: 'Corinth also left in 395 BCE because of the Corinthian War'; Corinth and Argos later merged their citizen bodies.
395: 'Thebes left in 395 BCE' and fought Sparta at Haliartus.
394: Cnidus ends Spartan sea power: 'the Spartan fleet was essentially wiped from the sea' and Spartan garrisons were expelled 'from several Ionian and Aegean cities'.
ledger.cp: Aegean cities of the former Delian League

ledger.x: 387: Corinth 'returned to Sparta under the King's Peace of 387 BCE'; 'Argos and Corinth ended their experiment in shared government'.
379: Olynthus brought into the league: members included 'Olynthos and Thrace, which had recently been conquered' (the Spartan campaign 'against it ran 382–379 BC').
378: 'Thebes left the Peloponnesian League for good in 378'; the Boeotian War (378–371) begins.
371: after Leuctra 'decisively shook its control of the League members' the Chalcidian cities are no longer Spartan allies; the page gives no year for their departure.
370: the Arcadians leave: 'The Arcadians left the League around 370 BCE to form the Arcadian League', founded around Megalopolis.
370: Mantineia, 'reconstituted after Leuctra', leaves with the other Arcadians for the Arcadian League.
369: the Thebans leave Laconia for Messenia and Arcadia; Sparta keeps Laconia.
369: 'Sicyon remained a member without interruption until 369'; Sicyon 'became allied to Thebes' in Epaminondas' second invasion.
331: Antipater's victory ends the war in the same year; no land changes hands.
225: Argos and Corinth go over to Cleomenes.
222: Argos returns to the Achaean League after Sellasia.
192: Sparta forced into the Achaean League.

wars.name: First Messenian War
wars.outcome: Spartan victory: Messenia conquered and its people reduced to helots.

wars.name: Second Messenian War
wars.outcome: The helot revolt crushed; Messenia stays Spartan.

wars.name: Battle of the 300 Champions
wars.outcome: Indecisive duel, then a decisive Spartan victory over the full Argive army; Sparta 'gained control of Thyreatis'.

wars.name: First Peloponnesian War
wars.outcome: Thirty Years' Peace (winter 446–445): 'Megara was returned to the Peloponnesian League', 'Troezen and Achaea became independent', Athens gave up 'all possessions in the Peloponnese'.

wars.name: Peloponnesian War
wars.outcome: 'Spartan victory'; 'Dissolution of the Delian League; Spartan hegemony over Athens and its allies'.

wars.name: Corinthian War
wars.outcome: The King's Peace 'dictated by the Achaemenid King Artaxerxes II in 387 BC': Asia Minor, Clazomenae and Cyprus to Persia; Lemnos, Imbros and Scyros to Athens; 'All other Greek cities were to be autonomous'; 'Thebes disbanded its league'.

wars.name: Boeotian War
wars.outcome: Theban victory at Leuctra (371), which 'decisively shook its control of the League members'.

wars.name: Theban invasions of the Peloponnese
wars.outcome: Messenia lost for good; the Arcadian League founded; the Battle of Mantinea (4 July 362) a 'Theban tactical victory' and 'Strategic draw' in which Epaminondas died.

wars.name: Philip II's invasion of Laconia
wars.outcome: Laconia devastated, border districts given to Sparta's neighbours, Sparta itself not taken; Sparta stayed outside the League of Corinth.

wars.name: War of Agis III
wars.outcome: Antipater's victory; Agis killed; no change of borders.

wars.name: Cleomenean War
wars.outcome: 'Achaean and Macedonian victory' at Sellasia (summer 222); 'Acrocorinth, Corinth, Heraea, and Orchomenus to Macedon'; Sparta confined to Laconia and occupied by Antigonus.

wars.name: War against Nabis
wars.outcome: 'Argos to the Achaean League, Laconian coastal cities become independent under Achean protection as League of Free Laconians'; an indemnity over eight years.

certainty.note: Ancient frontiers throughout; the Messenian border along Taygetus and the Thyreatis are the only named lines, and the pages give no survey.
